Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Acute onset lip angioedema progressing to respiratory compromise and dizziness within 30 min of prawn ingestion; prior atopy (peanut allergy, asthma); previous similar reaction after unknown food. No antihistamine or epinephrine available on scene.

Most consistent differential diagnoses (from DDx and transcript):  
• IgE-mediated anaphylaxis secondary to shellfish (prawn) exposure – High likelihood.  
• Allergic angioedema without systemic anaphylaxis – Moderate likelihood but less favored given airway symptoms/dizziness.  
• Hereditary angioedema – Low likelihood; no typical triggers/family history (DDx, conflict not present).

Working diagnosis: Suspected anaphylaxis triggered by shellfish.  

Management Plan

- Emergency management: Clinician initiated ambulance activation (999) for transport to ED.  
- Interim treatment: Instructed patient to take any available oral antihistamine immediately.  
- Airway safety: Advised patient not to remain alone; mother to stay until ambulance arrival.  
- Post-discharge follow-up: Patient to contact clinic after hospital visit for assessment of need for adrenaline auto-injector prescription, anaphylaxis action plan, and allergy referral.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to shellfish – High likelihood: Temporal relation to prawn ingestion, rapid progression, airway involvement, atopic history.  
2. Allergic angioedema without systemic features – Moderate likelihood: Lip swelling after allergen exposure but systemic signs make this less likely.  
3. Hereditary angioedema – Low likelihood: Recurrent swelling possible but food trigger and atopy favor IgE mechanism.
